children: Shares of Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. are in focus on Wednesday, November 25, the stock will trade adjusted for its buyback of shares today.

This means that those shareholders, who had shares of Zee Entertainment by the close of Monday's trading session in their demat account, will be eligible to tender their shares as part of the buyback process.
What Is The Zee Entertainment Buyback Proposal?

Zee Entertainment, on November 12 had informed the stock exchanges of its proposal for the buyback of up to 6.59 lakh fully paid-up equity shares of face value ₹1 each of the firm for up to ₹600 crore. The company said the buyback of equity shares represents 6.86% of the total paid up equity share capital of the firm.

The buyback price of ₹91 per equity share is payable in cash from the shareholders / beneficial owners of the equity shares of the company, as on the record date November 25, via the tender offer route, on a proportionate basis, the company said.
It has also appointed Emkay Global Financial Services as the manager to the buyback.
First ever buyback and shareholding pattern

This is the first instance of buyback in the company's history, as per data available on the stock exchanges. Prior to this, it has had just one bonus issue in the 1:1 proportion in November 2020. Meanwhile, it has been paying shareholders dividends every year since 2006.
At the end of the September quarter, promoter entities held 3.99% stake in Zee Entertainment Enterprises, while public shareholding comprised 96.01%, as per stock exchange data.

Zee Entertainment had said its board unanimously arrived at the proposal for buy-back of equity shares after deliberation of other key routes and the feedback shared by investors and shareholders. It recognized the buyback as an optimal approach to reward shareholders as well as reinstate confidence in its robust fundamentals and strategic roadmap for the future, the company said.

Zee Entertainment Chairman R Gopalan said that the decision to approve the buyback of equity shares reflected their confidence in the company's potential and fundamental strength to capitalize on the opportunities in the future. "The board believes that the company's intrinsic value is not appropriately reflected in its current market valuation and the buyback represents a prudent opportunity to reinforce confidence in the company's capabilities to generate long-term value for shareholders," Gopalan said.

Meanwhile, Zee Entertainment's CEO Punit Goenka said the company remains on a firm growth trajectory and the board's approval on the buyback of shares also reflects the company's potential and capabilities to capitalize on the opportunities ahead.

Shares of Zee Entertainment Enterprises ended the previous trading session 0.2% up at ₹71.55 apiece. The stock has risen 11.4% in the past month but has declined 13.5% in the last six months and 20.9% this year, so far.
